approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. It selects breeding parents by score band, then either makes a local mutation walk or joins connected fragments from two parents. Crossover independently cuts non-ring single bonds, usually retaining the larger first fragment and the smaller donor fragment; an optional finishing mutation can follow. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while ordinary mutation continuation remains active. Stable canonical identity and duplicate checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the archive and breeding population. This Parent retains the original unconditioned donor rule.
approach.novelty: Construct donors with reciprocal local attachment correspondence, excluding a cut from that conditional distribution when its valid immediate product exactly reproduces either generating parent. Keep the original relative cut weights, retain invalid alternatives under the existing failure rules, and fall back to the original donor draw when no conditional support remains. The preceding compatible-donor sibling often rebuilt a parent and relied on finishing mutation for novelty; it exposed some useful distinct recombinants but lowered final scores. This follow-up starts again from the unchanged Parent and revises that one construction law. It differs from selecting similar whole parents, preserving every first-parent ring, rejecting constructed mismatches, or changing posterior allocation or mutation continuation. It tests whether removing immediate parent copies exposes useful recombination, with no assumption that distinctness itself improves chemistry or endpoints.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-62daf219c70a has complete current-profile summaries and run logs: endpoint mean 0.5956696497334577 and seed-macro population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its crossover independently draws donor cuts without endpoint correspondence or a parent-copy-aware conditional law. The complete current removal n-767d2ce08797 loses 0.054937284705486644, so crossover presence remains supported; historical n-1faebb978a01 supplies a different-composition contextual control, not another current-profile replicate. The direct predecessor experiment n-eb61315a5619 correctly conditioned inherited donor mass on reciprocal context matches on 26727 informative attempts, but 22117 immediate products reconstructed a parent. Of 850 evaluated conditioned descendants, 496 acquired novelty only through finishing mutation. The remaining 354 nonidentical immediate recombinants included 257 pure crossovers, produced 70 strict best-parent beats and 32 incumbent gains, and 268 later served as parents. None of those informative nonidentical evaluations reached any median_2 session; this is an observed exposure gap, not proof that unchosen distinct support was absent. Total immediate-nonidentical crossover evaluations fell from Parent 1368 to 1023, even as all crossover evaluations rose from 1492 to 1549. Its complete mean fell by 0.020270634588430703, with seed changes -0.061941115197846064, +0.01964278148495091 and -0.018513570052396955; ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved. The targeted obstacle is conditional mass spent reproducing the actual generating parents, not failed execution or a proven explanation of the score loss. Excluding those products is untested and may remove useful mutation-mediated paths. The current ordinary-continuation removal n-dbee08307e86 also loses 0.02686763734135833, reinforcing preservation of that separate rule without establishing additive contributions or the value of finishing mutation. The earlier similarity and full-ring restrictions n-a20706504e8f and n-822f049d9c70 remain negative historical variants. The incomplete L07 hard gate n-7ba291681388 is only a predicate reference, and the n-32ac3137615b continuation-composition mapping stays partial.
hypothesis: Within reciprocal-compatible donor support, exclude cuts whose valid immediate product equals either generating parent, renormalize the inherited physical-cut and orientation masses, and use the original unconditioned donor law when revised support is empty or inapplicable.

finding_summary.headline: Copy exclusion exposes more distinct recombinants, but every seed mean falls
finding_summary.insights:
Removing immediate parent copies did expose a real, useful recombination channel, but solving that allocation obstacle did not make this donor refinement beneficial. Most crossover attempts still used inherited fallback, and more distinct evaluations did not preserve the complete search quality. This complete panel therefore supports a negative contribution from the revised donor law under the tested composition. It preserves the earlier negative compatibility-only result and the separate evidence that crossover itself contributes positively; it cannot isolate the incremental exclusion effect by treating the earlier sibling as the code Parent.

The chemical assessment makes clear why string distinctness is an incomplete target: evaluated descendants include very large repeated assemblies and difficult heterocycles, alongside useful compact amines and amides. A 110-heavy-atom repeated leader and a poorly scoring halogen-rich size tail coexist with stronger compact alternatives. These are observed limitations of selected chemistry, not proof that size or any one bond caused the loss. Local correspondence omits stereochemistry and remote functional relationships, and later mutations can change the matched environment.

The remaining attribution gap is which changed ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback led to the lower endpoints; unselected previews supply no counterfactual scores. Invalid-only and whole-fragment/exception branches must also remain distinct: atom-limit failures were naturally observed, while other failure controls were synthetic or source-only. The bounded follow-up has now returned another endpoint loss, so its registered review condition is met without turning the result into a broad anti-crossover, validity or safety conclusion.
finding_summary.results:
The registered exclusion worked on 747 states with both removable parent-copy mass and remaining support. On those same states, the earlier compatible-donor law would allocate an average 47.20% probability to a valid parent copy; the revised conditional law allocated zero. Independent reconstruction found no weight, predicate, sampling or preview/actual discrepancy. Compatible atom-limit products kept their probability mass: 139 were actually selected and failed through the inherited checks. Empty support remained common: 11,911 attempts had no compatible orientation and 18,031 were emptied by removing copies, so both used the original donor fallback.

The conditioned channel produced 4,459 valid immediate products distinct from both parents, 3,408 pooled descendants, 356 evaluations and 134 final survivors. Of the 356 evaluated descendants, 280 were pure crossovers and 76 had finishing mutation; 80 beat their best generating parent, 32 improved the incumbent and 264 later served as parents. Across all branches, distinct-immediate crossover evaluations increased from 1,368 to 1,610 and pure crossover from 961 to 1,122. Fallback still supplied 70 evaluated products made novel only after copying a parent and then mutating it. Coverage remained uneven: median seed 0 pooled 23 distinct conditioned products but evaluated none; seeds 1 and 2 evaluated 13 and 14.

All 15 task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.493017, a paired change of -0.102653 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.066514, -0.030336 and -0.211109; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and five improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.074022. More local parent beats, 695 versus 629, accompanied fewer incumbent gains, 249 versus 258, and weaker endpoints.

molecular.headline: Distinct recombinants include large repeated assemblies and strained heterocycles; compact amine and amide counterexamples remain
molecular.overall_character: The complete Child n-bddb1dbe8e32 panel is paired with code Parent n-62daf219c70a on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied frozen profile: child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatches. All thirty supplied trajectory files and corresponding Search logs were read; no trajectory or task is missing. Each node has 4,500 recorded evaluations, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task. The protocol reports means 0.49301691876777937 and 0.5956696497334577 for Child and Parent. These supplied outcomes and the differing runtimes do not establish activation or identify a chemical cause of the change. The evaluated output spans indole/azaindole carboxamides, very large repeated aza-aromatic dione assemblies, crowded oxygen/nitrogen polycycles, cyclic and flexible aryl amines, heavily halogenated ester/ketone assemblies, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 33, 38, 32 and 27, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. The common median of 33 in the second task hides a large tail: Child mean is 46 heavy atoms versus Parent 33.277011494252875, and one seed leader has 110 heavy atoms. Child ring-closure-string rates span 0.9655 to 0.9805 and aromatic-string rates 0.9598 to 0.9736. These count molecules bearing text features, not fractions of aromatic atoms or perceived ring counts. Ring and aromatic content are rich, with moderate diversity across seeds but recurring local families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and drug-likeness weak overall: conventional amines and amides coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, crowded bridges, unusual aromatic-labelled rings and excessive assembly size. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre markers in the digest. Protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres are nevertheless present; neutral notation does not prove absent basicity. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 size and ring readings in .slots/r0017-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json do not establish synthesis, conformation, stability or biological activity. The full trajectories, rather than only digest final_molecules from the last seed, support the seed-level comparisons below. Actual output provenance is separately joined in .slots/r0017-01-improve-L01/molecular/donor_exposure_audit.json. Across 34,540 Child crossover requests, 4,598 use conditioned support; 4,459 yield a valid immediate product distinct from both generating parents, 3,408 reach the temporary pool, 356 are emitted and evaluated, and 134 remain in the final populations. Of those 356 evaluated descendants, 280 have only crossover in their recorded operator list; the others include finishing mutation. Across all crossover branches, 1,610 evaluated products have distinct immediate identities and 70 start as a parent copy and become novel after finishing mutation, compared with 1,368 and 124 in the Parent. Parent immediate identities are reconstructed from the first finishing-mutation source or the unchanged raw checker identity; Parent cut/support receipts are absent, so its conditional, support-empty and whole-fragment exposures cannot be reconstructed from these logs. Child support is empty before exclusion on 11,911 attempts and emptied by copy exclusion on 18,031 attempts; these invoke inherited donor construction. No Child whole-fragment path was observed. Compatible preview entries include 24,600 confirmed valid parent copies excluded from conditional support and 753 atom-limit entries retained in support. Invalid-product and preview-exception statuses were not observed; their retained-support rule remains outside observed exposure. Thus the declared exclusion is only of confirmed valid immediate parent copies, not a general validity, global-novelty, scaffold-distance or chemical-quality guarantee. Unchosen previews have no scores and are not pool or evaluated molecules. All retained statements use observed feedback plus a score/serial retention replay checked against every batch receipt; ancestry is not endpoint attribution. The prior compatible-donor variant n-eb61315a5619 remains negative evidence: its supplied paired mean change was -0.020270634588430703, with ten task/seed decreases and five increases, despite real distinct recombinants and later useful descendants. Its absent informative evaluations in one objective did not establish absent unchosen support. The reused n-7ba291681388 predicate compares source-graph endpoint atom types and non-cut heavy-neighbor bond/type context, excluding hydrogen, isotope and stereochemical information. It supplies no complete functional-group or geometry preservation guarantee. That L07 gate evidence is incomplete, and the n-32ac3137615b continuation-composition mapping remains partial; neither establishes full-composition equivalence or transferable efficacy here. The gaps below preserve these conditions and counterexamples rather than assigning a descendant score to an individual cut.

per_task.generated_character: All three seeds concentrate near 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 retains an N-H indole linked to a pyridyl amide, with ring and amide chloromethyl substituents. Seed 2 leads with a 25-heavy-atom azaindole N-hydroxy anilide carrying N-chloromethyl and ring fluoromethyl groups; its fluorine and chlorine are carbon-bound. Seed 1 instead forms a 25-heavy-atom aryl-substituted fused four-/five-membered oxygen/imine system with an N-chloro amide and aryl thiol. The median remains the Parent's 25 heavy atoms, while the seed families differ from its N-halogen indole-amide, diketone and cumulene leaders. There are 68 evaluated conditioned descendants with distinct immediate identities, 36 finally retained; this is local chemical exposure, not proof of independent scaffold coverage.
liabilities: N-chloro amide bonds differ from carbon-bound halogens. Halomethyl substituents and N-O acyl-nitrogen chemistry need local assessment rather than a blanket halogen rule.
The four-membered oxygen ring fused to an imine-containing ring introduces geometry and stereochemistry questions.
A large early combined indole/amide assembly scores 5.3359431878781056e-08; retaining familiar fragments without suitable context does not ensure a useful molecule.
missing_features: Consistent conventional peripheral bond environments are not established among leaders: N-H indole and N-methyl alternatives exist, but chloromethyl substituents and N-chloro amides remain common in the cited high-scoring families.
The fused oxygen/imine family lacks demonstrated credible geometry and specified stereochemical identity. A valid small ring graph does not establish an accessible synthesis.
Chemically independent plausible alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are limited within each seed; different seed families prevent a global-collapse claim.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The compact Child azaindole N-hydroxy amide reaches 0.47189631731668286; several halomethyl-position variants tie at that value. Its ordinary N-methyl relative with a ring fluoromethyl group still scores 0.45530988925657906, so N-chloromethyl is not universally required. The seed-0 N-H indole/pyridyl-amide leader scores 0.45883631621439397 and seed-1 fused oxygen/imine leader 0.4458257099418776. A late 19-heavy-atom seed-1 relative retaining the N-chloro amide but losing the original pendant aryl organization scores only 0.00018047844347655518, and FBr scores 0.0. The visible association is compact aromatic/carbonyl organization and its substitution pattern, not N-halogen presence or atom count alone. The corresponding Parent seed leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081; two Child seeds improve and one declines while retaining distinct local chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled task median is 33 heavy atoms, but seed 0 has a 69.5-heavy-atom median and reaches a 110-heavy-atom leader containing repeated nitrogen-rich fused dione and aza-aromatic/biaryl units. RDKit perceives twenty rings in that leader, including small fused closures; this is a large repeated assembly, not a compact scaffold hop. Seed 1 instead reaches a 32-heavy-atom linked aza-aromatic carbonyl system with a carbon-linked nitrile and a chloromethyl-containing acetal/ether chain. Seed 2 leads with a 28-heavy-atom crowded bridged aminal/ether framework bearing a difluoroaniline, methoxy and C-O-Cl group. A close methoxymethyl analogue has no O-halogen bond. This differs from the Parent's compact 30-heavy-atom linked nitrogen heterocycle leader and its other cyanate/peroxide families. The task has 88 evaluated immediate-distinct conditioned descendants, 31 finally retained; the 110-heavy-atom seed-0 leader and seed-1 leader are direct pure-crossover examples. The seed-2 leader comes through inherited fallback after conditional support is emptied.
liabilities: Seed-0 leaders approach the graph atom bound and contain many linked/repeated aromatic units, carbonyl heterocycles and small ring closures, raising synthesis, solubility and geometry concerns without measured property evidence.
The best seed-2 string contains C-O-Cl, an oxygen-chlorine bond, rather than C-O-CH2Cl; it should not be conflated with an ordinary carbon-bound chlorine substituent.
The compact bridged family remains stereochemically unspecified even when the O-Cl bond is absent.
missing_features: Size-controlled recombination that preserves useful relationships without duplicating large aromatic/heterocyclic assemblies is inconsistent; the small high-scoring seed-2 family shows that large size is not required.
Geometrically credible and stereochemically defined versions of the crowded aminal/ether bridges are not demonstrated.

Conventional peripheral alternatives exist, but the selected leaders do not consistently avoid O-halogen bonds or chloromethyl ether motifs. Near-tied alternatives do not prove a universal replacement benefit.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, a small amide/hydroxamate cyclic-amine fragment 0.5087394957983193, and ethene 0.5. The 110-heavy-atom seed-0 leader reaches 0.6126113662774612, below the compact Parent seed-0 leader's 0.8561477222467935. Repetition and ring abundance alone therefore do not reproduce the Parent's favorable organization. Child seed 1 reaches 0.6171603393130302 versus Parent 0.6248206599713055. Child seed 2 reaches 0.6280623608017817 versus Parent 0.6178024026512013. Its methoxymethyl analogue scores 0.6279925724517541 and a pure conditioned trifluoroaniline relative 0.6270797851434561. The near-tie without O-Cl is a counterexample to any universal requirement for that bond. The record favors particular linked heterocycle/aryl arrangements and supports useful compact alternatives, without identifying one isolated bond as causal.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches a 28-heavy-atom N-methyl eight-membered diamine ring joined through a secondary amine and cyclohexenyl segment to a fluorophenol. Seed 1 reaches a 33-heavy-atom flexible polyamine/hydroxylamine-like chain between substituted aromatic regions, with multiple chlorines and an amino/methoxy phenyl group. Seed 2 stays with heavily chlorinated ester/ether/cyclohexenyl assemblies; its 39-heavy-atom leader has a pyridyl nitrogen but lacks the available aliphatic amines visible in the stronger seed-0/1 leaders. The task median rises from Parent 31 to Child 38 heavy atoms, with seed-2 median 65 and maximum 117; this describes the evaluated sample, not all molecular support. The Parent reaches flexible tertiary-amine and pyrrolidine/thioether families near the score ceiling. There are 83 evaluated immediate-distinct conditioned descendants, 27 finally retained. They include conventional-looking cyclic amines, but also sulfur/peroxide-bearing low-scoring large assemblies; immediate distinctness does not certify useful chemistry.
liabilities: Hydroxylamine-like N-O bonds, peroxides, crowded rings and unusual oxo/thioxo or S-H sulfur environments persist in evaluated and sometimes retained products.
Large halogen-rich ester/ether assemblies combine high molecular size with lipophilic aromatic surfaces without evidence of solubility, selectivity or stability.
The more recognizable amine families still contain multiple potential stereogenic centres and flexible or medium-ring geometries; a high supplied score is not a feasibility or activity measurement.
missing_features: The weak seed-2 leaders do not reproduce the available aliphatic-amine/aromatic arrangement present in stronger Child and Parent families. Such amines are already generated elsewhere, so this is uneven selected family coverage rather than a generator-wide amine absence.
The evaluated size tail lacks consistent simplification into useful compact alternatives; the successful 28-heavy-atom cyclic amine is a counterexample to requiring large halogenated assemblies.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the substituted cyclic diamines, benzylic centres and bridged structures remains unspecified; formal neutral notation does not resolve protonation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared low N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197. Child seed leaders reach 0.9369952876631162, 0.8060389689378349 and 0.0862962975393863, versus Parent 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. The high Child scores associate with available aliphatic amines placed alongside aromatic regions, whereas highly halogenated size-rich seed-2 structures remain low. This is a structural association, not an isolated amine causal test. A pure conditioned seed-0 cyclic-amine relative scores 0.9328016121837945. Changing one ring N-methyl to N-hydroxy in the leader gives 0.900386185259853. A retained conditioned-plus-append-atom sulfur/N-O polyamine scores 0.6819607146271867; a retained pure conditioned seed-2 peroxide/S-H oxo-sulfur assembly scores only 0.03122095729582554 despite beating its own generating parents. A late seed-2 molecule with an added aliphatic amino group still scores 0.0566402376019363. Adding nitrogen to that different framework does not recreate the stronger amine organization, and local parent improvement need not approach a strong endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The three leaders contain 28, 32 and 40 heavy atoms. Seed 0 forms a densely bridged aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl framework with medium rings; seed 1 combines an ethoxy/ethyl biphenyl region, cyclic tertiary amine and a four-membered aromatic-labelled N-N-N-carbonyl ring; seed 2 joins a substituted quinoline through an ether to a complex bridged nitrogen-dicarbonyl system. The task median rises from Parent 30 to Child 32 heavy atoms. Rings, aromatic surface and carbonyl/nitrogen functions remain abundant, with somewhat larger and more connected alternatives than the Parent's quinoline/bridged-dicarbonyl leaders. There are 27 evaluated conditioned descendants with distinct immediate identities and 12 finally retained. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders are pure conditioned products. Seed 0 has 34 valid-distinct-support attempts and 23 corresponding pool entries but zero evaluated conditioned descendants. Its evaluated absence therefore does not establish absent support or absent generated molecules.
liabilities: A four-membered aromatic-labelled ring containing adjacent nitrogens and a carbonyl raises a specific ring-chemistry concern, beyond simply counting heteroatoms.
Medium-ring and bridged architectures remain challenging structural proposals despite moderate atom counts and familiar carbonyl groups.
N-N and N-O functionality and unspecified stereochemistry remain present; a reciprocal local cut predicate does not validate these whole structures.
missing_features: Simpler plausible connectivities that preserve the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently represented among the selected leaders; the near-scoring saturated-ring alternative is an important counterexample to requiring the most unusual ring.
The many bridges, ring-bound unsaturations and N-N-rich ring systems lack demonstrated geometric and stereochemical identity.
Distinct compatible support is unevenly allocated into evaluations. The seed-0 pool witnesses prohibit interpreting zero evaluated conditioned descendants as missing generation capability.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329; the Child leaders score 0.21848482353485119, 0.2269659836567154 and 0.2161542124355421. The corresponding Parent leaders score 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. A new leading family can therefore exceed its same-seed Parent without a uniform improvement across seeds. A final seed-1 alternative with a saturated N-N-containing carbonyl ring scores 0.22507308754456207, near the aromatic-labelled four-membered-ring leader. The small unusual aromatic ring is not shown to be a universal requirement. A smaller cyclic amine bearing carbonyl and N(OH)2-like acyl-nitrogen substitution scores 0.1079857070483669, while methane scores 0.0. The visible association concerns combined aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl organization, not isolated carbonyl count, molecular size or ring count. The 40-heavy-atom final thioether-containing seed-2 relative scores 0.20441337548005672, below its retained leader.

per_task.generated_character: The Child leaders are compact at 25, 28 and 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 combines an aromatic-labelled nine-membered imino/carbonyl nitrogen ring, two N-F bonds, a fluoropropyl substituent and a phenolic aromatic system fused to a three-membered carbocycle. Seed 1 retains another aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring with N-methyl groups, a fluorinated cyclopentadienol and an unsaturated fluorinated oxygen heterocycle; its leader has no N-F bond. Seed 2 reaches a more compact fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen system with a thioether bridge, a pyridyl group and fluoroalkyl ether substitution, also without N-F. Median size remains Parent 27 heavy atoms. Four sampled Child molecules have a ring carbon bearing two double bonds, versus forty in the Parent; alternative difficult ring architectures and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Ninety evaluated conditioned descendants have distinct immediate identities and twenty-eight are finally retained; the seed-2 leader is a pure conditioned product.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader retains N-F bonds, a three-membered fused carbon ring and a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; string validity does not establish their joint feasibility.
The N-F-free seed-1 family still includes unsaturated/enolic small rings and the large aromatic-labelled ring, so removing one reactive bond does not settle overall plausibility.
Fluoroalkyl/ether and thioether-containing leaders have unspecified stereochemistry and untested conformational and tautomeric identity.
missing_features: Consistently credible ring geometry and tautomeric/conformational identity remain missing, even though the selected families use fewer cyclic cumulenes than the Parent.

Conventional nitrogen substitution occurs in high-scoring examples, but N-F still appears in the seed-0 leader; the evidence supports local alternatives rather than a universal fluorine or N-F requirement.
Stereochemically specified saturated fluorinated centres are absent, and no exact missing target pharmacophore can be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child leaders score 0.5675633414443552, 0.556658816594997 and 0.5457036398446661, versus Parent 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. Thus one Child seed improves using a family without N-F, while the other two decline. The Parent's strongest cyclic-cumulene leader is not reproduced as the strongest Child family. Changing the seed-1 leader's ring-bound fluorine to a fluoromethyl substituent gives 0.3797590229471195; local placement matters within that framework, rather than fluorine amount alone. A more elaborated seed-2 relative with an additional fluoroalkyl/ether N-substituent and longer sulfur-containing bridge scores 0.0021636918621293464; those multiple changes do not isolate one required feature. An early combined carbonyl/amide assembly scores 7.244639250726666e-27 and isolated F 1.1043196211273875e-26. Compact fluorinated polar organization is associated with higher scores here, but fluorination or nitrogen richness without context is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-bddb1dbe8e32, compared with complete matched n-62daf219c70a Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective under the frozen profile. One pure conditioned leader has 110 heavy atoms and repeated nitrogen-rich aromatic/dione units; another evaluated seed has median 65 heavy atoms while retaining low-scoring halogen-rich families. Compact bridged amines, amides and heterocycles also occur at high supplied scores, including a 28-heavy-atom cyclic diamine. Immediate distinctness and local compatibility therefore do not establish useful size or independent scaffold coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can produce distinct recombinants without controlling repeated scaffold assembly or excessive molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make preservation of learned functional relationships compatible with bounded structural elaboration and meaningful simplification. Assess complete molecular context rather than relying on difference from the two generating-parent strings. These observations do not justify a universal size cutoff, prohibit larger molecules, or establish that size caused the paired score change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Previously recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-bddb1dbe8e32 on the complete matched three-seed panel at 300 observations per objective. Evaluated or retained structures carry N-Cl, N-F, O-Cl, N-O, peroxide, halomethyl and unusual sulfur environments. Near-tied ether alternatives lacking O-Cl, N-methyl and N-H aromatic amides, and high-scoring N-F-free heterocycles are counterexamples to universal need for these bonds. The source-graph reciprocal predicate excludes hydrogen, isotope and stereochemical information and is not a whole-functional-group guarantee.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments across recombination and later mutations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide environment-aware local alternatives and preserve coherent functional groups while retaining favorable relationships learned from current-task feedback. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens, useful amines and conventional sulfur motifs need separate treatment from unusual local environments. Neither confirmed parent-copy exclusion nor the incomplete earlier gate evidence supports a broad validity, stability, synthesis or safety guarantee.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The ring-feasibility gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and recurs through n-62daf219c70a in the current n-bddb1dbe8e32 matched Search panel. Current leaders include fused four-membered oxygen/imine systems, an aromatic-labelled four-membered N-N-N-carbonyl ring, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings and a phenolic ring fused to a three-membered carbocycle. A saturated N-N carbonyl-ring relative scores near its unusual aromatic-ring leader, and recognizable cyclic-amine families remain useful. Fewer sampled cyclic cumulenes do not remove the other geometry concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid ring representation from credible small-ring unsaturation, aromaticity or bridged geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treat ring size, unsaturation, heteroatom arrangement and bridge connectivity as jointly relevant when offering alternative topologies. Preserve useful ring chemistry where supported instead of excluding all small, fused or bridged systems. Canonical validity, local endpoint correspondence and distinct parent identity cannot substitute for the missing geometric information, and no isolated score effect follows from these associations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Previously observed in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; all five current n-bddb1dbe8e32 tasks retain zero stereocentre-string incidence under the same three-seed observation budget. The molecules include substituted cyclic diamines, fluorinated carbocycles and complex aminal/ether bridges. The reciprocal donor key explicitly omits stereo information, while exact parent-copy comparison of the available strings does not add missing stereochemical content. Protonatable amines are present despite zero charge-string incidence.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged structures are emitted without specified stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry where molecular identity requires it, distinguishing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation and tautomeric state separately. These observations establish unspecified identity in the evaluated record, not a measured stereochemical penalty or an attribution to one graph operator.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-bddb1dbe8e32 on matched n-62daf219c70a Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective. One session has 34 attempts with valid distinct conditional support and 23 corresponding pool entries but zero selected evaluations, while other sessions evaluate and retain distinct conditioned products. Many selected leaders remain local variants or repeated assemblies. The earlier n-eb61315a5619 compatible-donor variant remains a negative complete-panel result despite distinct witnesses and useful descendants; its absent evaluated exposure did not prove absent support. Different seeds reach different chemical families, so this is not global collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generated local alternatives do not consistently become evaluated, chemically independent alternatives to the leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Track support, actual products, pool admission, allocation, accepted observations and retained descendants separately when diagnosing coverage. Seek feasible independent alternatives while preserving useful chemical context, and assess them through actual task-local feedback. Do not treat parent-string distinctness as scaffold novelty, pool absence as molecular impossibility, or ancestry as component contribution. The earlier L07 predicate and partial continuation mapping do not establish full-composition equivalence or an efficacy guarantee.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
